method: Official metro.pe 'Nuestras Tiendas' page (/stores, VTEX IO) loads its list client-side from https://www.metro.pe/files/store.json (70 entries, many with copy-pasted placeholder coordinates, some stale). Cross-checked with the public VTEX checkout API /api/checkout/pub/pickup-points swept around 48 Peruvian city centres (1 req/s): every physical Metro store is a seller with a 'Retiro en Sucursal' pickup point (codes H0xx hypermarkets / S0xx supermarkets) carrying geoCoordinates. 71 sellers found. Final list = 70 stores: all sellers except H007 'Metro Ingeniería' (= Metro UNI, Av. Túpac Amaru/18 de Enero, closed 2024-08-27 per peru-retail). Coordinates come from the seller pickup points (official retailer data) - store.json coordinates were not used because many are duplicated placeholders. Excluded store.json entries: 'Metro Sucre' (Av. Sucre 550, Pueblo Libre - no seller; the Sucre store closed ~2017 and was replaced by Plaza Vea per peru-retail 2018-03-06), duplicate second 'Metro Colonial' entry, and 'Metro Próceres' (SJL, same corner 'esq. Calle las Flores' as Metro Canto Rey, no own seller - treated as a duplicate of Canto Rey; verify). Reported count: Cencosud said 69 Metro supermarkets after opening Metro Las Lomas (Aug 2026); Cencosud corporate presentation (May 2026) shows 88 supermarkets in Peru for Wong+Metro combined. Our list has 70 (one more than reported) - the most likely stale entries are S100 'Metro Plaza del Sol' (Piura, not in store.json, no opening news found) or a closed store still configured as a seller. district/province/department come from the official address text (blank where ambiguous); a later stage should assign ubigeo by point-in-polygon.
